Conflict: Material and Design and Manufacture recommend post-consumer recycled polypropylene for low manufacturing energy, while In-Service rejects this due to its low impact resistance and instead recommends an aluminum alloy housing for maximum durability.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: Monomaterial Post-Consumer Recycled (PCR) PC/ABS blend without overmolding
Rationale: PCR PC/ABS provides the necessary impact resistance and structural rigidity (engineering feasibility) to withstand drops without the high carbon footprint and weight of aluminum, while avoiding multi-material overmolding ensures high-quality end-of-life recyclability.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: material durability and impact resistance vs end-of-life recyclability and low-carbon materials

Conflict: Manufacture recommends integrated snap-fits to eliminate auxiliary fasteners and simplify assembly, whereas In-Service and Circularity reject this because snap-fits are highly prone to breaking during disassembly, which severely hinders repairability.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Reversible threaded fasteners with metal threaded inserts
Rationale: While more complex to manufacture than snap-fits or direct plastic screws, metal inserts ensure the housing can be disassembled and reassembled multiple times for repair without stripping the threads, maximizing product lifespan.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing simplicity and speed vs ease of disassembly and repairability

Conflict: Material and Design and Manufacture recommend a brushed DC motor to avoid rare-earth magnets and complex electronics, whereas In-Service and Circularity reject this because brushed motors have a significantly shorter operational lifespan and lower energy efficiency.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with modular, non-glued neodymium magnets
Rationale: A brushless motor is essential for the tool's long-term durability and efficiency (engineering feasibility), and specifying modular, non-glued magnets allows for the recovery of critical rare-earth materials at end-of-life.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: avoidance of critical raw materials vs operational energy efficiency and product durability

Conflict: Material and Design and Manufacture recommend passive cooling via open ventilation slots to minimize weight and part count, whereas In-Service rejects this because open slots allow dust and moisture ingress that causes premature motor and electronics failure.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: Passive thermal management via internal aluminum heatsinks coupled to a sealed housing
Rationale: Since screwdrivers are frequently used in dusty environments, a sealed housing is critical for reliability (engineering feasibility), and using a mechanically attached internal heatsink avoids the unrecyclable nature of thermal potting compounds.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: material minimization vs environmental protection and component durability

Conflict: Manufacture recommends a monolithic integrated design to simplify the assembly line and reduce production waste, whereas In-Service and Circularity reject this because it makes individual component replacement impossible, forcing the entire tool to be discarded upon a single component failure.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play connectorized sub-assemblies
Rationale: This architecture balances assembly feasibility with sustainability by allowing easy replacement of high-wear components (like the trigger switch) and facilitating clean material separation at end-of-life.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing assembly simplicity vs ease of repair and end-of-life material separation

Conflict: Manufacture recommends corded AC power to eliminate the high environmental impact of battery manufacturing, whereas In-Service and Circularity reject this because a corded design lacks portability, which is the primary value proposition for the user.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack with screw-fastened casing (cobalt-free chemistry)
Rationale: Cordless operation is essential for market viability (engineering feasibility), and using a removable, standardized pack with cobalt-free chemistry (such as LFP) minimizes environmental impact while enabling battery replacement and circularity.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: elimination of battery environmental impacts vs product portability and battery circularity
